h: From coal mine to cycle centre
p: Here's a fact that might surprise you as you pedal past the lake: Hicks Lodge used to be an opencast coal mine. The whole site has been transformed as part of the National Forest, a huge project to plant millions of trees across a big chunk of Leicestershire, Derbyshire and Staffordshire, much of it on old mining land. Those young trees around you are part of that story, and the place will only get greener as the years go by.

A few tips to get the best out of it. If you're bringing little ones on balance bikes or stabilisers, the gentler routes around the lake give them plenty of confidence without any scary drops. Helmets are a must for everyone, and it's worth packing a puncture kit and pump if you're bringing your own bikes. Two or three hours is a good amount of time for most families, with a stop at the café in the middle.
Midweek and outside school holidays are calmer if you want the trails a bit quieter. On a hot day there isn't masses of shade on the newer sections, so sun cream and water bottles are your friends.

Make a day of it by heading to Moira, just down the road. Conkers is a big family discovery centre with indoor and outdoor play, and Moira Furnace is a restored early nineteenth-century blast furnace with walks along a restored stretch of the Ashby Canal. Between the three, you've got a full day out without straying far at all.
